title: Affine toric equivariant ideals and monomial restriction formulas
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $P$ be a fine commutative monoid with torsion-free group completion $G$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Write $k[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}ke^p$ and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}k[G]$ act on $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ by $\mu(e^p)=e^p\otimes e^p$ [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. For a monoid ideal $I\subseteq P$, allowing $I=\varnothing$, put $k[I]=\bigoplus_{p\in I}ke^p$. The maps $I\mapsto k[I]$ and $J\mapsto\{p\in P:e^p\in J\}$ are mutually inverse between monoid ideals and ring ideals $J$ for which $\mu(J)(k[P]\otimes_k k[G])=J\otimes_k k[G]$. They preserve finite generation in both directions. Moreover $k[I]=0$ if and only if $I=\varnothing$, and $k[I]=k[P]$ if and only if $I=P$.

For $a\in P$, the canonical isomorphism $k[P]_{e^a}\simeq k[P[a^{-1}]]$ sends $e^p/(e^a)^n$ to $e^{p-na}$ and carries the extended ideal to $k[I-\mathbf N a]$. For every homomorphism $h:P\to Q$ of fine monoids, extension to $k[Q]$ carries $k[I]$ to $k[h(I)+Q]$. These formulas agree under successive localizations and successive homomorphisms.

source.place: VIII 3.2.2 proof, 3.2.14 and Lemma 3.2.15, pp.103,105; finite-generation and extension formulas expanded by an agent.

proof.text: For any monoid ideal $I$, the support criterion [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-ideal-support] identifies $(e^i:i\in I)$ with the finite sums supported on $I$: the condition $p=q+i$ is equivalent to $p\in I$, since $I+P\subseteq I$ and $0\in P$. Thus this ideal is exactly $k[I]$. As $k$ is a field, the support of $e^p$ is $\{p\}$, so $e^p\in k[I]$ exactly when $p\in I$. In particular $k[I]=0$ iff $I=\varnothing$, and $k[I]=k[P]$ iff $I=P$.

source.place: VIII 3.2.14, p.105; support computation expanded using the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Put $A=k[P]$, $B=k[G]$ and view $J\otimes_k B$ as its image in $A\otimes_k B$. By the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], this image consists of finite sums $\sum j_t\otimes b_t$, $j_t\in J$; it is also the ideal generated by $j\otimes1$, because $(j\otimes1)(a\otimes b)=ja\otimes b$. For each $g\in G$, the bilinear rule $(a,b)\mapsto a\,\operatorname{coeff}_g(b)$ induces a linear map $C_g:A\otimes_kB\to A$, and $C_g(J\otimes_k B)\subseteq J$. If $\mu(J)(A\otimes_k B)=J\otimes_k B$ and $f=\sum c_pe^p\in J$, then $\mu(f)=\sum c_pe^p\otimes e^p$ lies in this image. The map $P\to G$ is injective by fineness [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], hence $C_p(\mu(f))=c_pe^p\in J$. For each nonzero $c_p$, multiplication by $c_p^{-1}\in k$ gives $e^p\in J$. This is coefficient extraction, valid also when $k$ is finite.

source.place: VIII Lemma 3.2.15 proof, p.105; explicit tensor-coefficient form of its grading argument.

proof.text: For an equivariant $J$, put $I_J=\{p:e^p\in J\}$. If $p\in I_J$ and $q\in P$, then $e^{p+q}=e^qe^p\in J$, so $I_J$ is a monoid ideal. Step 2 gives $J\subseteq k[I_J]$, and the reverse inclusion follows by summing scalar multiples of its defining monomials. Conversely, $\mu(k[I])$ lies in $k[I]\otimes_kB$, and that subspace is an ideal by step 2; thus its generated ideal contains $\mu(k[I])(A\otimes B)$. For the opposite inclusion, $e^i\otimes1=\mu(e^i)(1\otimes e^{-i})$ for $i\in I$, and every $j\otimes b$ is a finite sum of multiples of these elements. This proves equality of the two ideals. Together with step 1, the two assignments are mutually inverse.

source.place: VIII 3.2.14 and Lemma 3.2.15, p.105; the inverse-inclusion formula expands the source's obvious direction.

proof.text: If $I=E+P$ for a finite subset $E\subseteq I$, then the support criterion [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-ideal-support] gives $k[I]=(e^e:e\in E)$. Conversely suppose $k[I]=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Let $E$ be the finite union of their supports. Each $f_t\in k[I]$ has support in $I$, so $E\subseteq I$. Every $f_t$ lies in $(e^e:e\in E)$ by its finite expansion, while every $e^e$ lies in $k[I]$. The two generated ring ideals therefore agree. For $i\in I$, apply the cited support criterion to $e^i\in(e^e:e\in E)$: since its coefficient is $1\ne0$, it gives $i=e+q$ for some $e\in E$, $q\in P$. Thus $I\subseteq E+P$, and the other inclusion follows from the monoid-ideal property. Empty generating families give $E=\varnothing$ and are included.

source.place: VIII 3.2.14--3.2.15, p.105; finite-generation argument supplied by the agent.

proof.text: Let $Q=P-\mathbf N a\subseteq G$, as defined in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The inclusion $P\subseteq Q$ induces the coefficientwise map $A\to k[Q]$, and $e^a$ has inverse $e^{-a}$. Define on fractions $\Phi(f/(e^a)^n)=\sum_p c_pe^{p-na}$ when $f=\sum_pc_pe^p$. The fraction relation [def-weil-ring-localization-away] implies equality of these sums: apply $A\to k[Q]$ to the relation and cancel the invertible powers of $e^a$. In the reverse direction send $e^{p-na}$ to $e^p/(e^a)^n$ and extend $k$-linearly. If $p-na=q-ma$ in $G$, then $p+ma=q+na$ in $P$ (integrality), so the two fractions agree. This defines the reverse map independently of every monomial representation. The addition and multiplication formulas for fractions show both maps are ring homomorphisms, and their composites fix each fraction and each basis monomial respectively. This proves the stated canonical isomorphism.

source.place: VIII Proposition 3.2.2 proof, p.103; explicit construction of its localization isomorphism.

proof.text: Under $\Phi$, extension of $k[I]=(e^i:i\in I)$ is the ideal of $k[Q]$ generated by $e^i$, $i\in I$. The support criterion [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-ideal-support], now applied to $Q$, makes this the span of the exponents $I+Q$. These are exactly $I-\mathbf N a$: write $i+(p-na)=(i+p)-na$ using $I+P\subseteq I$, and conversely $i-na=i+(-na)$ with $-na\in Q$. Thus the extended ideal is precisely $k[I-\mathbf N a]$, including the empty ideal.

source.place: VIII Proposition 3.2.2 proof, p.103, and 3.2.14, p.105; ideal formula expanded by the agent.

proof.text: For any monoid homomorphism $h:P\to Q$, the induced $k$-algebra map sends $\sum c_pe^p$ to $\sum c_pe^{h(p)}$, collecting terms when exponents coincide. The extended ideal is generated by the images of its monomial generators, hence by $e^{h(i)}$ for $i\in I$. The support criterion [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-ideal-support] applied to the subset $h(I)\subseteq Q$ identifies this ideal with $k[h(I)+Q]$. No injectivity or torsion-free hypothesis on $Q^{\rm gp}$ is used: possible cancellations in images of sums do not change this generating set.

source.place: VIII Proposition 3.2.2 proof, p.103, and 3.2.14, p.105; explicit affine pullback formula supplied by the agent.

proof.text: For successive localizations at $a,b\in P$, either order sends a basis fraction to $e^{p-na-mb}$ and an ideal to $k[I-\mathbf N a-\mathbf N b]$. Repeated inversion of $a$ similarly combines the denominators by adding their exponents. For $P\xrightarrow{h}Q\xrightarrow{u}R$, the composite ring map sends $e^p$ to $e^{u(h(p))}$, and $u(h(I)+Q)+R=u(h(I))+R$, since $u(Q)\subseteq R$ and $0\in Q$. Thus the ideal extensions agree with the composite map. Finally the induced localization map $P-\mathbf N a\to Q-\mathbf N h(a)$ sends $p-na$ to $h(p)-nh(a)$; on rings it sends $e^p/(e^a)^n$ to $e^{h(p)}/(e^{h(a)})^n$, and both orders on ideals have exponent set $h(I)+Q-\mathbf N h(a)$. These basis and generator formulas prove all stated compatibilities.
